title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting UPDATE still unguarded — the dedicated guarded SQL is never wired into the handler and the race pin calls the SQL directly (vacuous)
evidence: Test (1729-1746): `pub fn wrong_person_awaiting_sql_has_taken_over_backstop_test() {` ... `// The dedicated guarded UPDATE 0-rows — the row is never yanked.` `let assert Ok(returned) =` `rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)` — the pin calls the guarded SQL FUNCTION DIRECTLY; it never drives the POST route. The handler still executes the unguarded writer — server/src/reference_checks/form_handler.gleam:1249-1258: `case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_wrong_person(config, row, id_uuid, token) False -> case sql.update_reference_call_status( config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated, )` — and update_reference_call_status.sql has no backstop: `WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status` (no taken_over_at clause; take_over_reference_call.sql writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at, status stays contact_initiated).
detail: Round-4 mandate condition 1: the executed wrong-person UPDATE carries no taken_over_at backstop (handler still calls update_reference_call_status at form_handler.gleam:1250); the guarded mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person is never called by any production code. Condition 2: the race pin is the exact vacuous shape the mandate forbids — it passes with the blocker live (the test suite is green @ df0ea22 WITH the hole open). A take-over landing between the token read and the UPDATE still yanks a landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction and dead-ends it.
recommended_fix: Wire mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person into apply_wrong_person's False arm (0 rows -> redirect); rewrite the race test to POST /reference/:token/wrong-person via router.handle_request with a take-over committed between read and UPDATE, asserting 303/stand-down; delete the direct-SQL pin.

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql + its generated sql.gleam function ship dead — the guarded query the blocker fix depends on has zero production callers
evidence: mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql: `UPDATE reference_call SET status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status, terminal_reason = 'contact_invalid', next_attempt_at = NULL, updated_at = now() WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'contact_initiated'::reference_call_status AND taken_over_at IS NULL RETURNING id::text;` — grep of the worktree: the only references to mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person are the generated module (sql.gleam:1891 `pub fn mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(`), the generated row type (sql.gleam:1875), the .sql source, and the test's two direct calls (integration test 1746, 1758). form_handler.gleam's apply_wrong_person (the wrong-person POST path) never calls it.
detail: The round-4 brief's orphan check: the guarded query + generated code ship without a single production caller; the handler's executed path remains the unguarded update_reference_call_status. The existence of the SQL file and its generated function is the entire r3 'fix' — it closes nothing.
recommended_fix: Either wire the function into apply_wrong_person (the blocker fix) or delete the SQL file + generated module; dead guarded SQL is worse than none because it makes the TOCTOU hole look closed.
